INDASA announced it has partnered with Save the Rhino International, a UK-registered charity working to safeguard rhino species and their landscapes. The partnership brings together two organizations connected by a shared symbol: the rhino.

For INDASA, the Rhyno has represented strength, resilience and performance for decades. For Save the Rhino International, the vision is a future where all five rhino species thrive in the wild. The idea is straightforward: the symbol that has represented INDASA for decades should also help protect the species behind it.

At the center of the initiative are INDASA’s Rhynogrip and Rhynostick White Line, both in 150mm and in 125mm. Throughout the campaign, these products will feature bespoke packaging designed to reflect INDASA’s commitment to the partnership with Save the Rhino International and to carry the conservation message to markets around the world.

The special-edition packaging becomes a visible platform for the conservation cause, placing it in the hands of the professionals who use these products every day. Every package sold also contributes directly to rhino conservation, creating a clear connection between a professional-use product and a global environmental cause.

Through its products, packaging, digital communication and international network, INDASA aims to raise awareness of rhino conservation beyond traditional environmental audiences, reaching the body shops and distributors where the cause has never been addressed before.

Save the Rhino International works in partnership with conservation organizations, governments and local communities to conserve rhinos and their landscapes. These collaborations bring together knowledge, expertise and resources to support evidence-based conservation, address the challenges facing rhino populations and secure their long-term recovery.

Through this partnership, INDASA is contributing to those ongoing projects and giving the conservation message a route into an industry outside the organization’s usual reach. The campaign gives industry professionals a way into the cause: by acquiring the products they already use in their surface preparation activities, they contribute to conservation efforts, creating a direct connection between product, people and purpose.

Running for one year, the campaign connects every package sold with a direct contribution to Save the Rhino International’s conservation work. For every campaign box sold, INDASA will donate €0.03 directly to the organization.

The campaign identity captures the connection at the heart of the partnership. “By The Rhyno” represents the means: the strength and reach of INDASA’s own symbol, put behind the cause. “For the Rhino” represents the purpose: raising awareness and supporting the conservation of rhinos and their natural habitats.

The donation matters. So does the attention it brings: rhinos placed in front of professionals who would otherwise never come across the cause, and the reminder that a routine purchase can be part of protecting a species.

The FutureTech Studio will return to the 2026 SEMA Show with more than 20 vehicles and a three-day education program highlighting technologies changing how automotive aftermarket products are designed, developed and brought to market. Topics include advanced powertrains and fuels, artificial intelligence, automated driving technologies and emerging product-development tools.

Located in Central Hall, booth no. 24401, FutureTech Studio will feature vehicles showcasing alternative fuels and EV powertrains, a FutureTech Live Education Stage offering 21 30-minute microlearning sessions across three days and product displays demonstrating solutions to help manufacturers get products to market faster.

“FutureTech Studio is designed to show industry professionals both where automotive technology stands today and where it’s headed, helping attendees evaluate emerging solutions, understand their business implications and identify opportunities to remain competitive,” said Jim Moore, vice president of OEM and product development for SEMA. “Attendees can expect a connected, hands-on environment where they can see technologies up close, talk with experts and experience how innovations are shaping the industry’s future.”

Moore, along with the SEMA Garage team, plays a central role in supporting technologies featured in the FutureTech Studio. SEMA Garage serves as an advanced R&D partner for the automotive aftermarket, giving companies access to engineering resources, testing capabilities and technical expertise to accelerate product development and navigate compliance. Its Los Angeles and Detroit facilities help manufacturers transform ideas into market-ready products. The exhibit connects that technical work with the products, systems and applications attendees can see on the show floor.

In addition to microlearning sessions in the FutureTech Studio, attendees can extend their learning through SEMA Education’s Vehicle Technology Track throughout the week in Upper North Hall. FutureTech Studio and related SEMA Education programming will address advanced powertrains, automated driving technologies and engineering tools.
- Featured vehicles include Bisimoto’s Nio EP9; Rezvani Motors; and Scorpion EV’s Project SENNA.

- Microlearning session: “Advanced Fuels and Propulsion: Accelerating the Future of Mobility,” Nov. 5 at 10 a.m. in the FutureTech Studio explores the potential of hydrogen internal combustion technology and its role in the future of vehicle propulsion.

- SEMA education session: “Advanced Fuels and Powertrains: Engineering the Next Generation of Vehicle Propulsion,” Nov. 4 at 11 a.m. in Room N259 highlights the rapidly evolving landscape of advanced fuels and powertrains, emphasizing a powertrain‑agnostic approach that supports innovation across the aftermarket.
- Highlights include displays of Sensor Field of View Mapping and Automated Driving Camera Perception.

- Microlearning session: “The Future of ADAS: Performance, Validation and Integration,” Nov. 5 at 10:30 a.m. in the FutureTech Studio examines the latest developments in ADAS technology, calibration, validation and vehicle modification.

- SEMA education session: “ADAS Unlocked: Ensuring ADAS Performance on Modified Vehicles,” Nov. 4 at 1 p.m. in room N255 explores the challenges and opportunities ADAS presents across the automotive ecosystem.
- ADAS Showcase education session: “ADAS and Vehicle Modification: An Open Industry Discussion,” Nov. 3 at 3 p.m. in the SEMA ADAS Showcase, booth no. 31200.
- Featured companies include Overland AI; GM Defense; Kuhnhausen Metal Concepts; Tinkegineering; and N+ Bikes.

- Microlearning session: “SAE Standards 101: From Creation to Industry Adoption,” Nov. 5 at 3 p.m. in the FutureTech Studio explores how SAE International standards are developed and why they play such an important role across the automotive industry.

- SEMA education session: “SAE International Standards: Shaping the Future of the Automotive Industry,” Nov. 5 at 9 a.m. in room N255 explores how companies can leverage programs to identify emerging talent, support workforce development efforts and recruit future employees.

“As vehicles become increasingly interconnected, it’s more important than ever for industry professionals to understand how emerging technologies will impact the future of driving,” said Luis Morales, director of vehicle technology for SEMA. “We look forward to delivering an experience that gives attendees practical insight into these changes so they can prepare their businesses for what comes next.”
